summary: The Playwright tests compile and use Playwright APIs correctly, preserving test case IDs and using valid asynchronous assertions. However, selectors contain placeholders and appear weak or guessed, e.g., 'product name', 'related product name', 'category badge', and 'brand badge', reducing reliability. Navigation URL checks use weak regex patterns without verifying unique product identity, risking false positives. Assertions rely on generic roles and text matching that may not be robust. No reusability or maintainability patterns such as page objects are employed.

issues.description: Selectors use placeholders like /product name/i and /related product name/i, which are not actual product identifiers and reduce test reliability.
issues.recommendation: Replace placeholders with real, stable selectors or test data-driven selectors. Avoid generic text matching for critical elements.

issues.description: Navigation assertions use weak regex patterns such as /.*product-detail/ that do not confirm that the correct product detail page is loaded.
issues.recommendation: Use more precise URL assertions or verify page content to confirm correct product detail page navigation.

issues.description: Assertions on generic roles like 'heading' or text like 'price' and 'category badge' may be insufficiently specific and brittle.
issues.recommendation: Use more specific locators or add contextual checks to increase robustness.

issues.description: No abstraction or page object pattern used; selectors and logic are duplicated across tests.
issues.recommendation: Consider using test fixtures or page objects to improve maintainability and reusability.

recommendations: Replace placeholder selectors with real, reliable selectors or parameterize tests with test data.
Enhance navigation checks to strongly verify correct page loading, e.g., by checking URL parameters or unique page content.
Use more specific selectors or add context around generic role or text selectors to increase test stability.
Introduce page objects or helper functions to reduce code duplication and improve maintenance.
